newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria launches probe into grain exports.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria launches probe into grain exports.

text.p: Bulgaria's prosecutor-general has launched an investigation into former agriculture minister Vassil Chichibaba and three of his deputies on possible criminal negligence charges over grain exports.

State news agency BTA said on Thursday Chichibaba and his deputies Manio Manev, Dimcho Shopov and Maria Bozukova "are suspected of authorising grain exports from the 1995 harvest without making due efforts to correctly calculate the country's grain needs".

In 1995 Bulgaria exported 827,280 tonnes of grain from the 1994-1995 harvest for 7.141 billion levs. A total of 198,933 tonnes of grain were subsequently imported for 6.456 billion levs to compensate for the shortage.
BTA said the four could face up to 10 years in jail if convicted.
Chichibaba was a former minister in the Socialist government of Zhan Videnov, who was toppled last month by mass street protests.
The interim cabinet which took office on February 13 vowed to bring to justice anyone found criminally responsible for the disastrous state of the economy.
The new government inherited an acute grain crisis dating back to the exports and compounded by a poor harvest last year.
